result.abstractText: The present retrospective study evaluated the supplementary value of gross tumor volume of the primary nasopharyngeal tumor (GTVnx) for overall survival (OS) risk stratification in patients with T3-4 nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC). A total of 118 patients with T3-4 NPC who received definitive intensity-modulated radiotherapy at Guilin People's Hospital (Guilin, China) between March 2020 and June 2025 were included. GTVnx was obtained from the radiotherapy planning system. A time-dependent receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve was used to determine the exploratory cut-off for predicting 3-year OS. Survival differences were assessed using the Kaplan-Meier method and log-rank test, and Cox proportional hazards models were used to evaluate the association between GTVnx and OS. Clinical and extended models were compared using the concordance index (C-index), Akaike information criterion (AIC) and time-dependent area under the curve (AUC), and sensitivity analyses were performed to assess robustness. The median follow-up time was 34.1 months and 18 deaths occurred (15.3%). The 36-month time-dependent ROC analysis identified 78 cm<sup>3</sup> as the exploratory cut-off for GTVnx, with an AUC of 0.709. Patients with high GTVnx had poorer OS than those with low GTVnx (log-rank P<0.001). In a multivariable Cox analysis, high GTVnx remained associated with poorer OS after adjustment for T stage and pretreatment Epstein-Barr virus DNA (EBV DNA; hazard ratio, 4.375; 95% confidence interval, 1.474-12.986; P=0.008). Adding GTVnx to the clinical model improved the C-index from 0.759 to 0.817, reduced the AIC from 135.151 to 133.085 and increased the 36-month AUC from 0.748 to 0.787. Sensitivity analyses supported the consistency of the main findings. GTVnx may provide supplementary prognostic information beyond T stage and pretreatment EBV DNA in patients with T3-4 NPC. However, the identified cut-off value and incremental prognostic value require validation in independent cohorts.
